newsitem.title: USA: Con Edison Q1 net hit 1995 rate agreement.
newsitem.headline: Con Edison Q1 net hit 1995 rate agreement.

text.p: Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc first quarter earnings were trimmed by the provisions of its 1995 rate agreement which accounted for $0.06 of the $0.09 drop in earnings per share, Chief Financial Officer Joan S. Freilich told Reuters Tuesday.
The remaining $0.03 was due to the weather, she said.

The utility, which serves New York City and the suburbs immediately north of the city, reported earnings per share of $0.69 for the latest quarter -- well below the $0.77 First Call consensus estimate and down from $0.78 earned in 1996.

The company said the earnings decline refelected the provisions of the 1995 electric rate agreement, which provided a lower allowed return on common equity and a lower level of incentive opportunities beginning in the second quarter of 1996; and the impact of the milder than normal weather in 1997, which resulted in lower stam revenues.
The first quarter of 1997 was almost 17 percent warmer than the first quarter of 1996, which was a colder than normal period, Con Edison said.
That "was a big contrast," Freilich pointed out in a telephone interview.

In last year's first quarter, she said, the utility's allowed return on equity was 11.1 percent and the rate agreement called for sharing returns over 11.6 percent with rate payers. The allowed return was 10.3 percent this year, with sharing triggered at 10.8 percent.
The change in allowed return reduced earnings per share $0.03, Freilich said, while the changes in incentives cost another $0.03.

Con Edison's settlement in New York's electric utility restructuring proceeding, now awaiting regulatory approval, allows a return on equity of up to 12.9 percent. Above that level, 25 percent of earnings will be used to lower rates and 25 percent will be used to reduce stranded costs.

The company said its first quarter electric sales volume, excluding off-system sales, decreased 0.2 percent from 1996's first quarter. Firm natural gas sales volumed decreased 12.5 percent and steam sales volume decreased 14.5 percent from the year ago quarter.
It said the volume decreases were primarily due to milder than normal winter weather in 1997's first quarter.
